newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire moves to fill Mobutu succession vacuum-TV.
newsitem.headline: Zaire moves to fill Mobutu succession vacuum-TV.

text.p: Zaire state television said on Monday political moves had started in parliament to elect a speaker who could be the constitutional interim successor to ailing and embattled President Mobutu Sese Seko.
It said Mobutu's close associate Mandungu Bula Nyati was endorsed by the steering committees of both the pro-opposition and pro-Mobutu party coalitions in parliament.
According to Zaire's transitional constitution, the speaker of parliament takes over the presidency in case of the incumbent's death or incapacity.
The post has been vacant since 1995 and Monday's designation of Mandungu must still be approved by a plenary session of the 738-member parliament.

Mobutu, 66, is battling cancer and has required treatment in Europe in recent weeks. But he has also lost control of more than half of Africa's third-biggest country to the rebels of Laurent Kabila and the United States has called for him to step down after 32 years in office.
"At the moment it is essential to find a speaker who could act as interim in case of a problem," Prosper Ndume, spokesman of the opposition USORAL alliance told Reuters.
